name: Genistein
short: 2-year trial, 389 postmenopausal women: more gut side effects on genistein (19% vs 8%), more dropouts. At 3 years: breast density, endometrium not significantly changed (138); thyroid unaffected (77).
text: In a 24-month randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in 389 postmenopausal women with low bone density, more women taking genistein (54 mg a day, in tablets that, like the placebo, also contained calcium and vitamin D) than placebo had gastrointestinal side effects (19% vs 8%) and discontinued the study; endometrial thickness did not change compared with placebo, and the authors note the study had limited power to evaluate adverse effects. In a subgroup of 138 of these women who continued for a third year, genistein did not significantly change mammographic breast density or endometrial thickness, there were no differences in discomfort or adverse events between groups; among the 77 who completed 3 years and had thyroid tests (40 genistein, 37 placebo), thyroid hormones and thyroid autoantibodies were unaffected. In a 6-month randomized trial in 20 postmenopausal women with metabolic syndrome, those taking genistein had no more adverse effects than with placebo and none discontinued. A 2021 report of in vivo and laboratory (in vitro) investigations says that people with mild to moderate psoriasis taking genistein had good tolerability, with no serious adverse events, discontinuations or dose-limiting toxicities; the abstract does not give the number of patients, the dose, the route or whether there was a comparison group. The 3-year follow-up abstracts describe the product as genistein aglycone; none of the cited abstracts studied soy foods. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
